episodes.181464: Deep seasonal moisture move northward over northern Arizona with numerous showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.181492: Afternoon surface heating combined with an embedded disturbance, which generated multiple strong to severe thunderstorms which lasted into the nighttime hours.
episodes.181581: A series of upper disturbances in the northwest flow combined with a surface trough/boundary led to the development of isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms in the late-afternoon and evening hours from the southern Piedmont and Sandhills into the northeast Piedmont and Coastal Plain. Storms became severe across Moore and Richmond counties, producing several reports of downed trees and power lines.
episodes.181616: A disturbance moving through along with low-level instability due to warm lake waters helped to spawn numerous waterspouts on Lake Erie in the afternoon. Many reports of waterspouts were received as most of the waterspouts occurred offshore of Buffalo and Hamburg.
episodes.182045: After a period of quiet weather, several days of strong to severe thunderstorms occurred during the latter part of July. Chinook was struck the hardest with up to baseball size hail resulting in significant vehicle and structural damage. Harlem and Fort Belknap also received severe hail. Additional severe storms impacted the east side of Great Falls, Belt, and Lewistown with large hail being reported in all three locations.
episodes.182074: A strong seabreeze thunderstorm caused trees to fall in Levy County.
episodes.182075: A seabreeze thunderstorm in Tampa Bay produced a strong marine wind gust.
episodes.182098: A mean westerly steering flow pushed a progressive Gulf sea breeze inland and pinned the Atlantic sea breeze between I-95 and the Atlantic coast in the afternoon where explosive convection developed over a very moist and unstable airmass. Additional strong to severe storms developed across SE GA near a meandering surface front, but coverage was limited given drier mean layer moisture.
episodes.182279: An upper level ridge extended from the Desert Southwest and south Texas northward to Nebraska and Wyoming. During the early to mid-morning hours, the temperature was in the mid to upper 60s and the dewpoint was also in the mid to upper 60s across south central Nebraska. In the early evening hours, the temperature was in the 80s and the dewpoint was in the mid 60s to lower 70s. There was subtle low to mid-level warm air advection/isentropic ascent across portions of eastern Nebraska during the morning hours. During the early evening hours, the effective wind shear was generally 40 to 50 knots and the most unstable CAPE was 3,000 to 5,000 J/kg. Mid-level lapse rates were generally between 7 to 8 degrees C/km. ||Storms developed and moved across south central Nebraska during the morning hours. One storm moved into Clay County and produced one inch hail just after 8 AM CDT. This storm weakened and moved out of the area later in the morning. Storms redeveloped across south central Nebraska during the afternoon hours. One storm strengthened and moved into Thayer County and produced one inch hail just after 7 PM CDT. This storm then moved southward into Kansas.
episodes.182280: An upper level ridge extended from the Desert Southwest and south Texas northward to Nebraska and Wyoming. Temperatures were mostly in the 90s during the early to mid-evening hours across north central Kansas. Dewpoints were in the upper 60s to lower 70s. There was a temperature gradient across northern Kansas with temperatures in the 70s and 80s across northeast Kansas and temperatures around 100 degrees in central Kansas. Effective wind shear was generally 30 to 40 knots across north central Kansas and most unstable CAPE was around 3,000 J/kg. Mid-level lapse rates were between 7 and 8 degrees C/km. Storms developed across north central Kansas during the afternoon hours. One storm developed and strengthened in Mitchell County and produced wind gusts estimated to be near 65 mph. This resulted in some minor tree damage. This storm then weakened and exited the area.
episodes.182632: Strong thunderstorms moving offshore produced wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.182744: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm developed along the Montana border in northern Campbell County and tracked southeast through far northeastern Wyoming. The storm produced large hail and very strong wind gusts to 80 mph, causing considerable damage in some areas.
episodes.182747: A severe thunderstorm produced wind gusts around 60 mph northeast of Morrisey.
episodes.182750: A thunderstorm became severe over southwestern Fall River County and then pushed southeast in Nebraska. The storm produced large hail south of Provo.
episodes.182751: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm tracked from Wyoming through portions of the central and southern Black Hills. The storm produced hail and wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.182963: Surface low pressure from eastern Montana into western North Dakota ushered moisture northward into western and central North Dakota which served as fuel for thunderstorm development. Although forcing for storm development was weak, enough was present to produce a supercell thunderstorm that moved south-southeast through Bottineau County. This storm produced winds that destroyed grain bins and severely damaged crops. Later in the evening additional thunderstorms developed over southwest North Dakota, with one producing ping-pong ball size hail in Bowman County.
episodes.183009: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.183122: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Kansas during the late afternoon and evening of the 30th. These thunderstorms moved southeast and across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the late evening. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183200: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over northeastern Oglala Lakota County, producing large hail to half dollar size in the Sharps Corner area.
episodes.183201: A severe thunderstorm produced wind gusts around 65 mph southwest of Batesland.
episodes.183202: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over southeastern Bennett County, producing large hail south of Tuthill.
episodes.183203: A thunderstorm briefly produced wind gusts around 60 mph in the Cactus Flat area.
episodes.183204: A thunderstorm briefly became severe south of Weston, producing hail near golf ball size.
episodes.183255: A disturbance moving through along with low-level instability due to warm lake waters helped to spawn numerous waterspouts on Lake Erie in the afternoon. Many reports of waterspouts were received as most of the waterspouts occurred offshore of Buffalo and Hamburg.
episodes.183335: A very hot and unstable air mass devolved into scattered afternoon thunderstorms. A few storms became severe after most locations topped 100 degrees.
episodes.183470: Supercells initially produced large to giant hail in northwest Nebraska during the evening of July 30, then grew upscale into clusters, resulting in wind damage in the central Sandhills.
episodes.183495: A cold front dropping south and outflow moving east from the NC coast collided across Robeson and Columbus Counties. The interaction of these features resulted in heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.183523: A strong thunderstorm complex known as a Mesoscale Convective System developed across southern Arizona and migrated westward into southern California during the evening and overnight hours on the 30th-31st. The mesoscale convective system developed in an environment characterized by MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/KG as well as around 30 knots of deep-layer shear from an inverted mid-level trough that was situated over northern Sonora in Mexico. Isolated damaging winds were reported in the Yuma area as well as a lightning induced fire in a tree farm located southwest of the City of Maricopa.
episodes.183524: A strong thunderstorm complex known as a Mesoscale Convective Complex, which developed across southern Arizona during the evening hours on the 31st, moved westward into southwestern Arizona and eventually into southeast California during the late evening and overnight hours on the 30th-31st. Strong outflow winds originating from the complex moved westward into the Imperial Valley resulting in severe wind gusts as measured by the main surface observing sites.
episodes.183526: The beginnings of a damaging wind event began to impact far southeastern Kansas before moving into southwestern Missouri.
episodes.183561: The ongoing active pattern lessened somewhat, but enough moisture and support remained to trigger isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms which resulted in a few instances of strong wind gusts and flash flooding.
episodes.183583: A weak front extended across SE GA while SW steering flow across NE FL brought a progressive west coast sea breeze inland through the afternoon. The sea breeze merger occurred near the St. Johns River basin and I-95 corridor. A few pulse strong to severe storms produced wind damage.
episodes.183600: An unusually strong upper level disturbance dropped southward from the northern Plains into western Missouri during the evening of the 30th and continued southward through the early morning of the 31st. Widespread wind gusts measured over 70 mph affected locations from Fort Scott to Lamar to South Springfield to Branson, resulting in widespread power outages from downed trees and powerlines. Some locations were without power for several days as a result of these storms.
episodes.183788: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail in Logan and Morgan counties.  Hail up to tennis ball size was observed in Logan County, with hail up to quarter size in Morgan County.
episodes.183789: Severe thunderstorms produced heavy rain, large hail and damaging wind across parts of Boulder, Denver, Elbert, Larimer and Weld counties.  One tornado touched down briefly near Carr, but no damage was observed.  Hail up to half dollar size was observed, along with peak wind gusts around 60 mph.  Heavy rainfall, up to 3.64 inches,  produced flooding and flash flooding around Fort Collins and Livermore in Larimer County.  Vehicles were stuck in up to 3 feet of standing water.  Water from heavy rainfall filled the lagoon and surrounding retaining walls near the Lory Student Center on Colorado State University's main campus in Fort Collins.  At least four buildings on campus were damaged by floodwater, university officials said.  In the Cameron Peak burn area localized flash flooding was observed.  Buckhorn Road was impassable from 1 mile east of Moose Ridge Road to Forest Road 129.  In addition, multiple mudslides forced the closure of Highway 126 in Jefferson County.
episodes.183830: Clusters of strong thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina during the evening hours ahead of an approaching cold front. A few of these thunderstorm clusters produced strong wind gusts along the coast and across the Atlantic coastal waters.
episodes.183836: Clusters of strong thunderstorms moved into southeast South Carolina from the South Carolina Midlands and southeast Georgia in the late afternoon hours ahead of a cold front. These thunderstorms then tracked to the east through the evening and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183866: A series of upper level low pressure systems over the SE United States contributed to an unstable atmosphere across South Florida, causing thunderstorms to form over the peninsula during the afternoon.
episodes.183879: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west across Pima and Pinal counties during the evening. Several power poles were downed on the Tohono O'odham Nation.
episodes.183889: Scattered storms produced numerous reports of wind and hail across the CWA.
episodes.183953: Severe weather made it into places near the Missouri border during the evening of the 29th. Trees were flattened at Ash Flat (Sharp County), Black Rock (Lawrence County), and Gamaliel (Baxter County). Early on the 31st, power outages were widespread in Boone and Marion Counties (due to lightning and wind). A shed was destroyed at Damascus (Van Buren County).
episodes.183977: A waterspout was observed well offshore the Lower Florida Keys in association with an isolated rain shower.  A tropical upper tropospheric trough was stationary to the east, over the central Bahamas.
episodes.184089: Extreme heat fueled storms that developed during the late afternoon. With the abundance of dry air aloft, these cells produced a microburst over Baton Rouge, causing extensive wind damage and injuring one person before dissipating after sunset.
episodes.184176: A thunderstorm over the area and put down and brought high wind from the Natrona County airport to Mills. Wind gusts as high as 68 mph were reported with the storm.
episodes.184251: Deep monsoon moisture continued to move across northern Arizona with strong to severe  thunderstorms.
episodes.184315: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine and produced high winds.
episodes.184516: On the evening of July 30th, a squall line moved south southeast out of SE Nebraska into eastern Kansas and western Missouri. This squall line produced widespread 60 to 70 mph wind gusts with a few gusts up to 80 mph.
episodes.184517: On the evening of July 30th, a squall line moved south southeast out of SE Nebraska into eastern Kansas and western Missouri. This squall line produced widespread 60 to 70 mph wind gusts with a few gusts up to 80 mph.
episodes.185202: A weak pressure pattern led to seabreeze-driven showers and thunderstorms over interior South Florida. Light winds caused the storms to move little, producing very high rainfall rates.
episodes.186576: A surface high pressure ridge built over Lake Erie from the Upper MS Valley during the morning of the 31st and was accompanied by a land breeze convergence zone just north of the OH shore. The relatively-strong updraft of a cumuliform cloud along the convergence zone spawned a brief non-mesocyclonic waterspout amidst sufficient low-level moisture and lake-induced instability offshore Vermilion.

Lightning from a Monsoon thunderstorm destroyed a house in Baderville, north of Flagstaff Monday. Summit Fire and Medical crews arrived at the home just after 12:30 p.m. on a report of the roof of the home on fire. As crews got closer to the scene, firefighters could see smoke from Highway 180 and the fire was moved to a first alarm. Initial crews arrived to find heavy smoke coming from the attic of the home. More crews arrived to work the fire, including two water tenders. In all a total of 11 units and two battalion chiefs responded to the fire. There were no injuries to civilians or fire personnel and the home is a total loss (KAFF Country News).

Minor street flooding was reported along DeBarry Avenue. This is a known flood prone location.
The Treasure Coast International Airport KFPR ASOS measured a 36 knot wind gust from the south.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree across Byfaul Avenue in Baker.

events.narrative: Weatherflow site XIND in the Indian River near Grant measured a 34 knot wind gust from the northwest.
The Vero Beach Municipal Airport KVRB ASOS measured a 39 knot wind gust from the northwest.
Lake Okeechobee South mesonet site L001 reported a wind gust of 41 kts or 47 mph            associated with a thunderstorm.
The Treasure Coast International Airport KFPR ASOS measured a 36 knot wind gust from the east-southeast.

Capitol Reef National Park reported flash flooding associated with thunderstorms in the area, which necessitated the closure of several roads in the park, including portions of the Scenic Drive, The Capitol Gorge Road, and Pleasant Creek.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted or snapped trees and a tin roof was blown off.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree on a house in Broadmoor area.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree in the Old Goodwood subdivision of Baton Rouge.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree onto a home with 3 people inside. No injuries reported.
A structure at 84 Lumber collapsed due to thunderstorm winds seriously injuring 1 person.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree onto a powerline in Jefferson Terrace subdivision in Baton Rouge.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree on the corner of Forest and Sholar drives.
A patio roof blown off by thunderstorm winds in Oak Hills subdivision of Baton Rouge. Report relayed via social media.
A few snapped trees, one uprooted, and minor metal roof damage from thunderstorm winds at BR Proud News studio.
A tree was downed by thunderstorm winds near intersection of Highland Road and Know Hill Drive. Relayed via social media.
A mobile home had the tin roof partially peeled off.
A spotter relayed a picture that showed a mixture of dime, nickel, and quarter sized hail.

As much as 6 to 9 inches of rain fell in the Port LaBelle area during the late afternoon and early evening of July 31st, leading to street flooding. Cowboy Way was closed for several days from Birchwood Parkway to NW Raintree Blvd. No structures were impacted. ||The flooding continued into the first few days of August, and is also included in the August StormData publication.
Large tree branches were snapped in a severe storm.
Lake Okeechobee West mesonet site L005 reported a wind gust of 36 kts or 41 mph            associated with a thunderstorm.
Trees were downed between Maurice and Milton.

Seven empty hopper style grain bins were blown over, and one empty standard style grain bin was also destroyed. Various trees were damaged, with some smaller trees broken off. The wind was also accompanied by up to one-inch diameter hail and caused extensive crop damage in the area.
Two hanger doors at Chris Crusta Memorial Airport received minor damage. A tree was also downed near by.
Horry County Fire Rescue was dispatched to a residential structure fire on Ashboro Ct.
The combination of large hail and gusty winds produced some property damage.
The strong thunderstorm winds combined with small hail to strip a nearby corn field down to its stalks.
Large branches were broken from a thunderstorm.
Heavy rain produced multiple mudslides on and near Highway 126.  The roadway was closed until the debris could be cleared.
A tornado touched down briefly in open country near Carr.  No damage was reported.
